reason: Conversation 1 gives a correct, honest and complete safety stop in one turn: do not use, the crack compromises insulation and exposes live parts, engineer to replace the glass, no DIY repair. Conversation 2 reaches the same stop and does get the homeowner to switch off at the wall, but it pads this with irrelevant checks (error codes, feeling the surface for loose shards on a cracked energised hob), then pastes a washing-machine-style boilerplate about plugs, sockets and 'the machine' that doesn't fit a hardwired hob and ignores the cooker switch she just mentioned. It also gives misleading model-label advice (the oven's door-seal sticker is not the hob's) and steers toward self-sourcing a part before any engineer assessment. Conversation 1's main gap is not explicitly saying to isolate at the cooker switch and neither mentions insurance, so the edge is only slight.
